items.title: Accordion Icons: Which Work Best?
items.summary_original: So what icon is the most reliable to show expansion and collapsing for accordions? Is there really any noticeable difference between carets, chevrons, arrows, and triangles? Well, research shows that there is some difference indeed. But what’s more interesting is that split menus are harmful , why it's better to not have icons and text labels link to different actions, and why the caret is the safest icon choice. Let’s dive in! No Icon = Opening The Page The findings aren’t very surprising: without any icon in use, users expect that tapping on the menu item would take them directly to a new page. Users often struggle with custom icons as they don't clearly signal that they'll open an accordion. And people tend to tap fairly equally on the icon and on the label for most icons. Many designs

items.summary_de: Welches Symbol zeigt also am zuverlässigsten die Erweiterung und Reduzierung von Akkordeons an? Gibt es wirklich einen erkennbaren Unterschied zwischen Carets, Chevrons, Pfeilen und Dreiecken? Nun, Untersuchungen zeigen, dass es tatsächlich einen gewissen Unterschied gibt. Interessanter ist jedoch, dass geteilte Menüs schädlich sind, warum es besser ist, keine Symbole und Textbeschriftungen mit verschiedenen Aktionen zu verknüpfen, und warum das Caret-Symbol die sicherste Symbolwahl ist. items.summary_original: Alice Bucknell’s The Alluvials In 2023, artist Alice Bucknell released The Alluvials, a video work filled with wolves, moths, and sediment that looks at a version of Los Angeles in the near future. In this California city, the sand that had once been characteristic of its beaches has taken over downtown, effectively turning the sprawl of highways and skyscrapers into a desert of dunes and dust. Through this speculative lens on an alternate reality, Bucknell presents both the history and consequences of this dried-up world. The work examines the history of the Tongva people of the Greater Los Angeles Basin while also imagining the water desalination corporation Qwench, a perpetually burning landscape, and an eternity in which the sky remains in its golden hour. items.title: we drove volvo’s electric EX60 to russel wright’s modernist woodland home at manitoga
items.summary_original: an autumn drive into the hudson highlands Volvo ‘s new all- electric EX60 took us from Manhattan to Manitoga, the woodland home of American industrial designer Russel Wright in Garrison, New York. The drive north brought us out of the city and into the tree-lined roads of the Hudson Valley, glowing with autumn color, where the Swedish automaker had organized a design experience around its newest electric SUV. During the mid-twentieth century, Wright spent decades transforming a former quarry into a 75-acre woodland estate. The experimental and iconic modernist home incorporates the surrounding forest into its architecture, with the resulting space feeling like an architect's fairytale. items.title_de: Wir fuhren mit dem elektrischen EX60 von Volvo zu Russell Wrights modernistischem Waldhaus in Manitoga
items.summary_de: Eine Herbstfahrt in die Hudson Highlands Der neue vollelektrische EX60 von Volvo brachte uns von Manhattan nach Manitoga, dem Waldhaus des amerikanischen Industriedesigners Russel Wright in Garrison, New York. Die Fahrt nach Norden führte uns aus der Stadt hinaus auf die von Bäumen gesäumten Straßen des Hudson Valley, die in Herbstfarben leuchteten, wo der schwedische Autohersteller ein Designerlebnis rund um seinen neuesten Elektro-SUV organisiert hatte. Mitte des 20. Jahrhunderts verbrachte Wright Jahrzehnte damit, einen ehemaligen Steinbruch in ein 75 Hektar großes Waldgebiet umzuwandeln. Das experimentelle und ikonische modernistische Haus bezieht den umliegenden Wald in seine Architektur ein, und der daraus resultierende Raum wirkt wie ein Architektenmärchen. Die Designer von Volvo haben ähnliche Ideen für den EX60 erforscht und dabei natürliche Materialien und andere Materialien untersucht

items.title: Celebrating 20 Years of Open Movies
items.summary_original: This year we are celebrating 20 years of making Open Movies. 17 titles, all different and beautiful in their own way. We want to thank you for being a part of this journey – without the community support, all of these projects would not be possible! To celebrate the 20 years of Open Movies in a special way during the Blender Conference 2026, we have created an installation that represents the projects frame by frame. And in the spirit of sharing and being open, visitors of the exhibition can take a frame with them. 20 years of Open Movies exhibition at Blender Conference 2026 Thank you for doing your part. Let’s see what the next decade of open filmmaking will bring!

items.summary_original: HERZOG & DE MEURON REVEALS EAMES INSTITUTE MUSEUM PLANS A warehouse with a roof this expressive already has something to exhibit. In Novato, California, Herzog & de Meuron is reworking the former Birkenstock campus into the future museum of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity, preserving its sculptural concrete silhouette while changing what happens beneath it. Newly released renderings show the proposal taking shape with San Francisco practice EHDD as executive architect and Field Operations designing the landscape. Across an approximately 88-acre site, the project brings exhibition spaces, workshops, a theater, and gardens into a cultural destination whose ambitions extend beyond the work of Charles and Ray Eames . The existing campus was designed for publisher McGraw-Hill by Jan L

items.summary_de: HERZOG & DE MEURON ENTHÜLLT MUSEUMSPLÄNE DES EAMES INSTITUTE Ein Lagerhaus mit einem derart ausdrucksstarken Dach hat bereits etwas auszustellen. In Novato, Kalifornien, gestalten Herzog & de Meuron den ehemaligen Birkenstock-Campus zum künftigen Museum des Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity um, indem sie seine skulpturale Betonsilhouette bewahren und gleichzeitig das Geschehen darunter verändern. Neu veröffentlichte Renderings zeigen, wie der Vorschlag Gestalt annimmt, wobei das Büro EHDD in San Francisco als ausführender Architekt fungiert und Field Operations die Landschaft gestaltet. Auf einem etwa 88 Hektar großen Gelände bringt das Projekt Ausstellungsräume, Werkstätten, ein Theater und Gärten in ein Kulturziel, dessen Ambitionen über die Arbeit von Charles und Ray Eames hinausgehen. Der bestehende Campus wurde von Jan L. für den Verlag McGraw-Hill entworfen

Jeff Sauro, PhD and Jim Lewis, PhD found that UX job postings are down 71 percent from their 2022 peak, and research postings are down even further. They also found that one in three organizations cut UX staff in a single year, the worst reading on record, worse than the one right after the 2008 financial crisis. items.title_de: Die KI-Abrechnung in UX hat 20 Jahre gedauert
items.summary_de: Das Feld ist in zwanzig Jahren dreimal explodiert und wieder aufgebaut worden. Dies ist der dritte. Jeder denkt, dass KI wegen Design kommt. Die Wahrheit ist hässlicher und älter. Das Feld hat sich das schon zweimal angetan, und es wird es wieder tun. Der UX-Arbeitsmarkt ist derzeit wirklich düster. items.title: these glowing amber sculptures begin with a natural polymer produced by tiny insects
items.summary_original: insects make the material for ori orisun merhav's sculptures Brussels-based designer Ori Orisun Merhav is experimenting with a natural polymer produced by tiny lac insects , transforming their resinous secretions into glowing sculptures and sculptural furniture. Through her research practice Made by Insects, she heats and blows the amber-colored material into clusters of translucent bubbles, some perched on branching steel structures, others suspended as elaborate chandeliers. The material is known commercially as shellac, a substance typically used as a protective coating. Here in Merhav's hands, it takes on a completely different spirit. Her latest works extend the research into 3D printing and large-scale installations, imagining how an insect-produced material might become part of our
items.title_de: Diese leuchtenden Bernsteinskulpturen basieren auf einem natürlichen Polymer, das von winzigen Insekten produziert wird
items.summary_de: Insekten bilden das Material für die Skulpturen von Ori Orisun Merhav. Der in Brüssel ansässige Designer Ori Orisun Merhav experimentiert mit einem natürlichen Polymer, das von winzigen Lac-Insekten produziert wird, und verwandelt ihre harzigen Sekrete in leuchtende Skulpturen und skulpturale Möbel. Im Rahmen ihrer Forschungspraxis Made by Insects erhitzt und bläst sie das bernsteinfarbene Material in Ansammlungen durchscheinender Blasen, von denen einige auf verzweigten Stahlkonstruktionen sitzen, andere als kunstvolle Kronleuchter aufgehängt sind. Das Material ist im Handel als Schellack bekannt, eine Substanz, die typischerweise als Schutzbeschichtung verwendet wird. Hier in Merhavs Händen bekommt es einen ganz anderen Geist. Ihre neuesten Arbeiten erweitern die Forschung auf 3D-Druck und großformatige Installationen und stellen sich vor, wie ein von Insekten produziertes Material Teil unseres Lebens werden könnte

items.title: mcdonald’s recycles happy meal toys into wireless mouse shaped like french fries
items.summary_original: MCDONALD’S AND LENOVO PUT FRENCH FRIES ON THE DESKTOP McDonald’s China is giving its fries a place beside the keyboard. Developed with Lenovo, the brand’s French fry-shaped wireless mouse translates its familiar red carton and yellow contents into a computer accessory, incorporating plastic recovered from old Happy Meal toys. The collaboration brings together two recognizable features of the fast-food experience: the packaging that holds lunch and the small plastic object that tends to outlast it. This time, the latter gets something useful to do. The design keeps the visual shorthand intact. A red lower shell carries the Golden Arches, while molded yellow fries rise across the top, giving the mouse an uneven silhouette that departs from the anonymous curves of conventional office hardware

items.summary_original: VITREON STEEL EXPANDS LAUFEN’S ARCHITECTURAL UNIVERSE LAUFEN introduces VITREON steel, a new material that redefines the architectural possibilities of contemporary bathroom spaces. By uniting the strength and malleability of steel with the temper, chemical resistance, and non-porous gloss of glass, the material establishes a versatile new baseline for premium washbasins. The result is extraordinarily durable, scratch-resistant, color-fast, and fully protected against corrosion while maintaining a high standard of hygiene. Beyond its physical performance, VITREON steel enables refined geometries, paper-thin wall profiles, and a tactile finish that engages directly with light. items.summary_original: a speculative approach to interspecies design Ulster University researcher and designer Alan Hook develops Equine Eyes, a giant horse-shaped headset that allows people to experience an approximation of how horses see the world. The wearable forms part of his wider research into interspecies design, which explores how objects and environments might be designed with other animals in mind. What happens when the animals that share our spaces are considered users too? With its elongated white muzzle and upright ears, the headset has a peculiar, almost cartoonish appearance. Small cameras sit on either side of the head, where a horse's eyes would be, while a virtual reality display translates their live footage for the human wearer. The experience is deliberately playful, inviting participants t

items.summary_de: Ein spekulativer Ansatz für das Design von Interspezies. Der Forscher und Designer Alan Hook von der Universität Ulster entwickelt Equine Eyes, ein riesiges pferdeförmiges Headset, das es Menschen ermöglicht, eine Annäherung daran zu erleben, wie Pferde die Welt sehen. Das Wearable ist Teil seiner umfassenderen Forschung zum Interspezies-Design, bei der erforscht wird, wie Objekte und Umgebungen unter Berücksichtigung anderer Tiere gestaltet werden könnten. Was passiert, wenn die Tiere, die unsere Räume teilen, auch als Nutzer gelten? Mit seiner verlängerten weißen Schnauze und den aufrecht stehenden Ohren hat das Headset ein eigenartiges, fast cartoonartiges Aussehen. Kleine Kameras sitzen auf beiden Seiten des Kopfes, wo sich die Augen eines Pferdes befinden würden, während ein Virtual-Reality-Display ihre Live-Aufnahmen für den menschlichen Träger übersetzt. It describes the cognitive tendency to rely excessively on a familiar tool or method and to apply it (sometimes compulsively) to any problem. This tendency can run counter to a design-based, research-oriented approach, as it often leads to similar results. Against the backdrop of the growing power of technology companies, interdisciplinary, conceptual, and thus research-based design is becoming increasingly important—with regard to a cohabitation that is increasingly characterized by (visual) communication and language. items.summary_original: When speed disguises itself as progress. One driver worked hard to get to a stoplight. (Rounded Bevel Icons) I distinctly remember my father driving the speed limit down a two-way street in the Bronx when a car swung out from behind us and cut into our lane with a few feet to spare. It wasn’t the first time, and whenever it happened, I’d anticipate his favorite phrase, delivered with zero road rage, “Going nowhere fast.” Twenty seconds later, we rolled up to a red light, with the car that cut us off sitting right next to us. One question that stayed with me as a curious 12-year-old: “ Did they notice? ” Did the driver notice that, after all that effort to get ahead, their reward was a red light? items.title: emma sicher grows biomaterials from wild berries and microorganisms
items.summary_original: emma sicher grows materials with microbes Berlin-based biodesigner Emma Sicher is experimenting with materials grown by bacteria and yeast, turning microbial cellulose into everything from translucent packaging to edible food prototypes. Some of her samples resemble crinkled pieces of pink glass, while others form glossy, gelatinous spheres. Their unusual colors and textures emerge through fermentation, a process in which microorganisms help produce the material itself. At the center of her practice is SCOBY, a symbiotic culture of bacteria and yeast commonly associated with kombucha. As the microorganisms grow in a nutrient-rich liquid, cellulose-producing bacteria form a gelatinous membrane at the surface. items.summary_de: Emma Sicher züchtet Materialien mit Mikroben Die Berliner Biodesignerin Emma Sicher experimentiert mit Materialien, die von Bakterien und Hefen gezüchtet werden, und verwandelt mikrobielle Zellulose in alles, von durchscheinenden Verpackungen bis hin zu essbaren Lebensmittelprototypen. Einige ihrer Proben ähneln zerknitterten rosafarbenen Glasstücken, während andere glänzende, gallertartige Kugeln bilden. Ihre ungewöhnlichen Farben und Texturen entstehen durch Fermentation, einem Prozess, bei dem Mikroorganismen dabei helfen, das Material selbst zu produzieren. Im Mittelpunkt ihrer Praxis steht SCOBY, eine symbiotische Kultur aus Bakterien und Hefen, die häufig mit Kombucha in Verbindung gebracht wird. Diese können geerntet und zu flexiblen Folien verarbeitet oder zu anderen verarbeitet werden

Wir sprechen von einer variablen Schriftart, an der fünf Jahre lang gearbeitet wurde, einer humanistischen Sans-Schriftart, die für Legastheniker entwickelt wurde, einer Displayschrift, die aus Tonabdrücken von Grabsteinen zusammengesetzt ist, und einer geometrischen Schablone, die durch Ziehen einer variablen Achse zwischen scharf und abgerundet wechseln kann. An anderer Stelle steckt Eleganz in einer neuen Version

items.title: Socialist Hotels: relive the concrete dreams of the Soviet era with these beautiful photos
items.summary_original: A new photo book documents the hospitality architecture behind the Iron Curtain. We all dream of staying in a luxurious hotel fit for royalty. Most of us settle for something half-decent, as long as it's affordable. Either way, we don't really expect to be surprised by the architecture: these days, even the best hotels are largely about uncomplicated functionality. So imagine booking a room for the architecture, and finding a building shaped like a flying saucer, a giant snowshoe or a typewriter. Well, that's the world captured in Socialist Hotels, a new book from FUEL . Featuring photographs by Elena Amabili, this is apparently the first photography book to focus solely on hospitality architecture in Eastern Europe and the post-Soviet landscape.
